A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCIREAS/KRUX study. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and section relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original frontier-model evaluations, controlled fine-tuning and knowledge-injection experiments, and benchmark-validation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds alternative-extractor experiments, reasoning-budget subgroup results, and curation-agreement results.

M1.justification: The KRUX extraction/injection procedure, knowledge-probing approach, and SFT objective remain unchanged. The expanded KI definition already appears in v1's extraction prompt. Qwen3 is tested as an alternative extractor configuration; SCILIT01 and its training recipe remain in Appendix E.4.

E1.justification: The training mixtures, ten-benchmark suite, and probing tasks are retained. Corresponding domain inventories—v1 Tables 11–14 and v2 Tables 13–16—list identical subtasks and instance counts. The added analyses partition or reuse existing task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 2 adds Qwen3-235B-A22B to the frontier-model comparison. New Tables 11–12 compare Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 with DeepSeek-R1 as extractors. Existing post-training comparators remain; Table 10's Qwen3-SYNTHETIC-1 column is renamed SCILIT01.

E3.justification: New protocols compare extractors using matched source traces and a blind 100-pair audit, and measure low-to-high reasoning-budget gains using micro accuracy over 8,527 Has-Math and 4,757 No-Math cases. Existing training, sampling, and decoding settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends validation by testing extractor dependence on GPQA and MMLU-Pro*, auditing paired KI outputs, and examining whether frontier-model reasoning-budget gains depend on mathematical content. It also adds independent curation-agreement analysis. These address distinct robustness and validation questions beyond v1's retained analyses.

E5.justification: New Figure 10 reports 95% confidence intervals for math/non-math reasoning-budget gains, extending uncertainty reporting to these contrasts. The existing five KI permutations, means and standard deviations, and 30-sample benchmark-validation analysis remain unchanged. No increased run count or new interval-estimation procedure is specified.

E6.justification: Existing performance values in Tables 1–7 and 9–10 are unchanged. Added results include 90.1% curation agreement, frontier subgroup gains, and alternative-extractor scores. For example, v2 Table 11 reports Qwen GPQA accuracy of 35.0 with self KIs and 43.5 with R1-source KIs under Qwen3 extraction; these are additional configuration results.

T1.justification: The standard SFT negative-log-likelihood objective is identical in v1 Appendix D.1 and v2 Appendix E.1. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or substantive formal assumption is introduced; the expanded KI description restates existing prompt content.

C1.justification: The benchmark and KRUX contributions and the three central knowledge/reasoning claims retain their meaning. SCILIT01 disappears from the abstract and introductory emphasis, but its training contribution and findings remain in Appendix E.4 rather than being withdrawn.

C2.justification: Appendix F.2 newly interprets the extractor comparison as evidence that KRUX generalizes across extractors and discusses differences in KI granularity. Section 3.2 connects reasoning-budget benefits to mathematical content. Existing knowledge-retrieval caveats and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 expands curation documentation with annotator roles, validation steps, candidate counts, and UGPhysics recall-only filtering, without establishing that existing evaluations were rerun. It specifies the KI audit sample, adds Qwen3 pricing, and changes SYNTHETIC-1-SFT's 'Trained by Us' entry from Yes to No. Core hyperparameters and repository access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds CURIE and QASA and explains their limited suitability for the study's knowledge/reasoning isolation goal. v2 also adds the Sprague math/CoT discussion, revises faithfulness references, and removes the Qwen3 technical-report citation. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the abstract and conclusion, expands curation and KI explanations, and reorganizes the math analysis. The training-contribution section moves to Appendix E.4 and limitations to Appendix A. Most of the scientific narrative and existing explanatory prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Document-wide reformatting changes the title block, running headers, caption placement, and appendix layout, including wider prompt and example boxes. v2 adds Figures 10 and 16 and Tables 11–12, expands Figure 2, and updates Figure 4's labels. These are extensive visual changes beyond pagination.

improvement.justification: The alternative-extractor validation and more explicit curation documentation improve confidence in and reproducibility of the retained central results. The gain is limited: added documentation contains a SciKnowEval L3-and-above versus L5-only ambiguity, and Figure 10 does not explain its confidence-interval calculation. Nevertheless, the targeted validation provides a modest net improvement.
